brief: UBS's weekly outlook covers three threads. US nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August versus a 55,000 consensus, with private payrolls up 127,000 and revisions adding 55,000 to prior months, lifting the three-month private-payroll average to 75,000, above the 0-60,000 breakeven range. That, plus a more hawkish Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and recent inflation data, shifted UBS's base case from the Fed staying on hold to two 25bps hikes, in September and December. UBS says this does not change its positive equity outlook, since the same resilience supports both. This week's CPI and PPI will test whether inflation cools enough to temper the Fed's hawkish turn. On Europe, headline inflation rose to 3.3% in August from 2.9% on energy costs, but core (2.4%) and services (3.0%) eased and PMI hit 52.7. UBS expects Thursday's 25bps ECB hike to be followed by an extended pause, not a sustained tightening cycle, and stays Attractive on Eurozone equities. On AI, Broadcom raised its fiscal 2027 AI-chip revenue forecast to about $115bn from over $100bn and sees $230bn in fiscal 2028. UBS says investors should retain AI exposure but diversify across the value chain, with Oracle's Thursday results as the next demand test.
